title: Sensex Surges Over 1,200 Points Intraday As Crude Falls, FIIs Buy
excerpt: Live snapshots on November 11 put the Sensex up 1,280 points at 9:53 a.m. before trimming gains by afternoon, with Kalyan Jewellers rallying over 12% on results and RVNL also higher intraday.
body:
• Intraday on Wednesday, November 11: at 9:53 a.m. the BSE Sensex traded at 82,386.84, up 1,280.19 points or 1.58%, and the Nifty 50 at 25,388.05, up 343.40 points or 1.37%, according to Outlook Money — these are live figures, not closing levels.
  • By 12 noon the Sensex was up 1,272.72 points at 82,379.37, before trimming to 81,961.89, up 855.24 points, at 1:11 p.m., The Hindu BusinessLine's live blog reported.
  • Kalyan Jewellers rallied over 12% to a fresh high after reporting a 64% rise in consolidated profit after tax to Rs 427 crore for the September quarter; RVNL was also higher intraday, trading at Rs 209.50, up 3.87%, at 2:01 p.m. on Dhan's NSE feed.
  • For diaspora investors, the drivers named by sources were falling crude, a stronger rupee and foreign buying — FIIs invested Rs 53,739 crore in Indian equities in the first nine days of November, Outlook Money reported citing NSDL data.

Indian benchmarks surged in early trade on Wednesday, November 11, as markets reopened after the November 10 Diwali-Balipratipada holiday. At 9:53 a.m., the BSE Sensex was trading at 82,386.84, up 1,280.19 points, or 1.58%, while the NSE Nifty 50 gained 343.40 points, or 1.37%, to trade at 25,388.05, Outlook Money reported. During early trade the Sensex rose to an intraday high of 82,520.40 and the Nifty touched 25,424.35.

The gains did not hold at their peak all session. By 12 noon, the Sensex had climbed 1,272.72 points, or 1.57%, to 82,379.37, with the Nifty up 341.35 points, or 1.36%, at 25,386, according to The Hindu BusinessLine's live blog. By 1:11 p.m. the same live blog had the Sensex at 81,961.89, up 855.24 points, or 1.05%, and the Nifty at 25,270.25, up 225.60 points, or 0.90%. Readers should treat every level in this report as an intraday snapshot at the time stated, not a close.

Why the market rose

Outlook Money named three supports: a sharp correction in crude oil prices, heavy buying by foreign institutional investors, and hopes of easing geopolitical tensions in West Asia. Brent crude futures for January delivery fell 1.44% to an early trade low of $90.75 per barrel on November 11, compared with the previous close of $92.08, it reported. Lower crude eases concerns over India's import bill and inflation.

Foreign buying was the second leg. FIIs have turned net buyers in November, investing Rs 53,739 crore in the first nine days of the month, according to data from the National Securities Depository (NSDL) cited by Outlook Money, after remaining net sellers in September and October. The rupee also appreciated 0.17% against the US dollar to trade at Rs 93.76 on November 11 at 11:48 a.m., Outlook Money reported.

Midcaps, Kalyan Jewellers and RVNL

Breadth was broad. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 advanced between 1% and 2% in early trade, Outlook Money said. Separately, MarketsMojo reported the BSE Midcap segment up 1.17% on the day, with 123 stocks advancing against 25 decliners, and Kalyan Jewellers leading the pack with a 12.11% gain, while Cochin Shipyard fell 6.40%.

BusinessLine's live blog gave the reason for Kalyan's move: its shares rallied over 12% to a fresh high on Wednesday after the jewellery retailer reported a 64% year-on-year increase in consolidated profit after tax to Rs 427 crore for the September quarter of FY27.

Rail Vikas Nigam (RVNL), named in the Business Standard live coverage that prompted this report, was also trading higher intraday. Dhan's NSE feed had RVNL at Rs 209.50 at 2:01 p.m., up 3.87% from its previous close of Rs 201.70, after an intraday range of Rs 202.72 to Rs 220.32. That is a live price snapshot, not a closing price.

What to watch next

BusinessLine listed results due on November 12 from companies including Oil India, Vodafone Idea, NMDC and Alkem Laboratories, which MarketsMojo also flagged as the next midcap catalysts. For now, the story of November 11 is an intraday, post-holiday rally led by banking, auto and broader-market buying — final closing levels will differ from the snapshots reported here.
